questions.prompt: What was the main problem with early studies of bilingual children?

options.text: They used too few participants.
They did not take social background into account.
They tested children only in their stronger language.
They were carried out by untrained researchers.

questions.explanation: They 'compared children from poor immigrant families with wealthier native speakers'; the disadvantage vanished when researchers 'control[led] for social background'.
questions.trap: C is the opposite: they were tested in their WEAKER language.

questions.prompt: According to the second paragraph, why might bilingualism improve executive function?

options.text: Bilinguals learn to read earlier.
Bilinguals must keep inhibiting one language.
Bilinguals spend more time studying.
Bilinguals use only one language at a time.

questions.explanation: 'must constantly suppress the language that is not needed'.

options.text: the brain's ability to delay the effects of damage
a type of memory used for languages
a treatment for Alzheimer's disease
the number of languages a person can learn

questions.prompt: What does 'publication bias' mean in this passage?

questions.explanation: 'experiments that find an interesting effect are more likely to be … accepted'.
